title: Haslet
name: Haslet
metaDescription: 1031 exchange coordination for Haslet, TX investors, where logistics and distribution growth near AllianceTexas requires rail-easement and entitlement documentation.

sections.html: Haslet sits on the far north side of Fort Worth, immediately adjacent to the AllianceTexas development, and its commercial growth over the past decade has followed the same logistics and distribution demand that built out the Alliance corridor itself. An exchange buyer here should expect industrial and flex product with rail and easement documentation questions specific to a fast-growing logistics submarket.

sections.heading: Haslet's Position In The Alliance Logistics Corridor
sections.html:
Haslet's commercial base has grown along Business 287 and the rail lines running through the area, driven largely by spillover demand from the AllianceTexas industrial park just to the south. Distribution and warehouse buildings, along with the smaller flex and service buildings that support them, make up a growing share of what is available, much of it built within the last several years.

Because so much of this development is recent, an exchange buyer should confirm the current status of any rail spur easements, BNSF right-of-way agreements, or shared-access agreements tied to a specific building, since these instruments are common in a rail-served logistics corridor and are not always fully recorded at the time a building is first leased.

Residential growth has followed the same logistics-driven expansion, with Eagle Mountain-Saginaw ISD serving much of the area, and that rooftop growth has in turn brought a small but growing base of retail and service tenants along Business 287 that did not exist a decade ago.

sections.heading: Property Types Available In Haslet
sections.html:
Haslet's inventory reflects its position inside the broader Alliance logistics footprint.

  • distribution and warehouse buildings with rail-served access
  • light industrial and flex buildings serving logistics tenants
  • service and retail buildings along Business 287
  • land parcels recently entitled for industrial or distribution use

Confirming which category applies to a given candidate early sets realistic expectations for the diligence timeline, since a rail-served warehouse typically carries a longer document list than a straightforward retail building on Business 287.

sections.heading: Where A Generic Exchange Scope Misses Haslet
sections.html:
A quote written for a retail-driven Fort Worth suburb rarely addresses the rail easement and right-of-way documentation that a logistics building in Haslet requires. A properly scoped diligence list confirms rail spur easement terms, any BNSF or Union Pacific right-of-way agreement affecting the parcel, and clear-height, dock-door, and power-capacity specifications that a lender underwriting an industrial building will expect to see documented rather than estimated.

It should also confirm whether the parcel's entitlement for industrial or distribution use has fully cleared any required zoning hearings, since some Haslet land was rezoned from agricultural use relatively recently.

A generic scope also tends to overlook whether a building's lease is structured around a single logistics tenant's specific dock configuration, which can make the space harder to re-lease to a different operator without modification, a detail worth surfacing before the property is treated as a straightforward income-producing asset.

sections.heading: Coordination Sequence For A Haslet Candidate
sections.html:
Once a Haslet property is under contract, the identification file should confirm rail easement status, building specifications, and entitlement history before the lender's underwriting proceeds, since industrial financing typically requires more documentation upfront than a standard retail loan. The qualified intermediary should be notified as soon as the purchase agreement is signed so funds are positioned ahead of the 45-day identification deadline.

Because rail easement confirmation can take longer than a standard title search, that request should go out the same day the property is added to the identification list rather than after it becomes the leading candidate, leaving enough of the window to resolve any question before day 45.

sections.heading: What The Haslet Identification File Should Contain
sections.html:
A complete file documents any recorded rail spur easement or railroad right-of-way agreement, confirmed clear-height and power-capacity specifications, current zoning and entitlement status, and a title commitment confirming no unresolved restrictions tied to the parcel's recent development. Assembling this before the deadline keeps the exchange coordination on schedule.

For a building leased to a logistics or distribution tenant, the file should also note the remaining lease term and any renewal or termination option, since a shorter remaining term changes how a lender treats the income stream when exchange proceeds are financed against the property.

faqs.q: Why does a Haslet industrial building need rail easement review?
faqs.a: Many Haslet logistics buildings are rail-served, and spur easements or railroad right-of-way agreements are not always fully recorded at the time a building is first leased, so confirming their status is a standard diligence step here before the property is identified.

faqs.q: What building specifications matter most for a Haslet industrial candidate?
faqs.a: Clear height, dock-door count, and power capacity should be confirmed directly rather than estimated, since lender underwriting for an industrial building relies on documented specifications rather than marketing figures.

faqs.q: What kinds of properties are available to buy in Haslet?
faqs.a: Distribution and warehouse buildings with rail-served access, light industrial and flex buildings, service and retail buildings along Business 287, and recently entitled industrial land.

faqs.q: Should recent rezoning be confirmed before identifying a Haslet property?
faqs.a: Yes. Some Haslet land was rezoned from agricultural to industrial or distribution use relatively recently, and confirming that the process fully cleared all required city hearings avoids an unresolved land-use question surfacing later during underwriting.

faqs.q: How is Haslet connected to the AllianceTexas development?
faqs.a: Haslet sits immediately adjacent to AllianceTexas, and much of its recent logistics and distribution growth reflects spillover demand from that larger industrial park to the south.
